NetBrain appoints three new executives to help customers chart their path to Agentic NetOps.

Jun 30, 2026

Luvlynn Lee, Sean Dolan, and Scott Fitzgerald join as CCO, CRO, and CMO as enterprise network operations teams move from evaluating AI to deploying it

BURLINGTON, Mass., June 30, 2026 - NetBrain Technologies, the pioneer of Agentic NetOps, today announced three executive appointments: Luvlynn Lee as Chief Customer Officer (CCO), Sean Dolan as Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), and Scott Fitzgerald as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO).

The appointments are the latest in a deliberate sequence of moves. Following Blackstone's majority investment and Bernadette Nixon's appointment as CEO in January 2026, NetBrain is now building the customer success, revenue, and marketing leadership to match the scale of the opportunity. Enterprise network operations teams are under compounding pressure: alert volumes are growing, headcount is flat, and the gap between detection and diagnosis and resolution is where business impact lives. The technology to close that gap operationally is production-ready. The leadership build-out reflects a direct investment in getting customers there.

"Our customers are navigating a pivotal moment. They know AI will transform their network operations and they are looking to NetBrain to show them the path. Bringing Luvlynn, Sean, and Scott into the leadership team is a direct investment in that promise and will make us a stronger company. Luvlynn will ensure every customer has a clear and supported journey to Agentic NetOps, Sean will extend that journey to the enterprises who have not yet discovered what autonomous network operations can do for them, and Scott will make sure the market understands what is now possible."

Bernadette Nixon, Chief Executive Officer, NetBrain Technologies

Luvlynn Lee - Chief Customer Officer.

Lee brings more than 20 years of experience building and scaling customer success, sales, and go-to-market functions at high-growth technology companies. Most recently, she served as Chief Revenue Officer at Split Software. Prior to Split, she held senior commercial leadership roles at Teradata and earlier at ThousandEyes, the cloud intelligence platform acquired by Cisco, where she helped double annual recurring revenue in two years. Her career has been defined by a consistent ability to turn early customer relationships into scalable, referenceable programs - precisely the operating model NetBrain needs as Agentic NetOps moves from early adopters to mainstream enterprise deployments.

"What drew me to NetBrain is the rare combination of proven technology and a genuinely uncharted category," said Luvlynn Lee, Chief Customer Officer at NetBrain Technologies. "Agentic NetOps is a fundamentally different way of running a network, and most enterprises are still discovering what it means for them. My job is to be the partner that helps them see the path clearly, take the first step confidently, and realize value faster than they thought possible."

Sean Dolan - Chief Revenue Officer.

Dolan joins NetBrain with an extensive background in enterprise technology revenue leadership, including his most recent role as Chief Revenue Officer at EnterpriseDB. His career includes senior positions at Qlik, Juniper Networks, Alcatel-Lucent, and Nokia Worldwide Services, giving him deep credibility in both the networking infrastructure market and the broader enterprise software go-to-market motion. Dolan is known for building structured, scalable sales organizations that can navigate complex enterprise buying cycles, and activate partner and channel ecosystems to extend market reach, a critical capability as NetBrain expands across new verticals and geographies.

"Network operations will be genuinely transformed by AI, and that creates a significant market opportunity for a company that has done the hard work of building real agentic capability - and NetBrain has," said Sean Dolan, Chief Revenue Officer at NetBrain Technologies. "My focus will be on making sure we are translating technical leadership into commercial momentum."

Scott Fitzgerald - Chief Marketing Officer.

Fitzgerald brings over 20 years of enterprise technology marketing leadership. Most recently he led marketing at Intapp, the governed AI platform for highly regulated industries, through an IPO and tripled their ARR. Before that, he held CMO and SVP roles at Duck Creek Technologies, BlueSnap, ACI Worldwide, and CA Technologies. He specializes in connecting brand, go-to-market strategy, and demand generation to deliver growth for software-as-a-service companies.

"Enterprise networks are at an inflection point, and NetBrain is the platform built to meet it," said Scott Fitzgerald, Chief Marketing Officer at NetBrain Technologies. "My job is to make sure the enterprises that need Agentic NetOps can find it, understand it, and act on it."

About NetBrain Technologies.

NetBrain is the pioneer in Agentic NetOps, delivering autonomous network operations through AI agents that diagnose, decide, and act with full network context. NetBrain serves approximately one third of the Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 across the most complex enterprise networks in the world, with offices in Boston, London, Munich, Hyderabad, Beijing, and Toronto.

NetBrain achieves Infoblox certification to advance real-time netops.

8th June 2026

Network automation and AI specialist NetBrain has become a certified Infoblox partner for real-time netops.

David Mann, vice-president of global services at NetBrain, said the Infoblox network identity operating system (NIOS) certification expanded its capabilities.

"This is a powerful, validated and future-proof integration," Mann said.

"Together, NetBrain and Infoblox give teams synchronised operational intelligence across configuration, topology, and DDI data."

For example, better managubg domain name system (DNS), dynamic host configuration protocol (DHCP), and internet protocol (IP) data.

Infoblox served as the system of record. However, NetBrain acted as the "system of reality" validating live network behaviour, the vendor said.

Real-time netops for greater observability.

Network operations (netops) teams need more capabilities for modern hybrid networks, Mann suggested. Netops teams could use the integration for network intelligence, automation and validation.

For example, NetBrain retrieved subnet, IP range, DNS and DHCP data automatically from Infoblox NIOS.

"This data seeds and accelerates network discovery, ensuring NetBrain's digital twin is always aligned with the authoritative source of truth," the vendor said.

In addition, NetBrain's network maps were dynamically enriched with Infoblox data, giving visibility of hostnames, IP lease statuses, and other DNS/DHCP attributes directly on the topology.

Also, when running automated diagnostic workflows (Runbooks), NetBrain can validate DNS resolution, DHCP availability and IP address allocation in real time. There's also path and configuration analysis.

US-based NetBrain offers agentic netops tooling. The idea is for teams to use a live digital twin, intent-based automation and AI to deliver observability, including troubleshooting automations.

NetBrain builds out agentic AI operations capabilities: AutoCon 5 preview.

NetBrain has been building agent-driven network operations capabilities on top of its network discovery and network visibility platform. In early 2026, the company debuted two AI agents: Deep Diagnosis and Runbook Companion. This May, NetBrain introduced new capabilities including a feature called AI Path Doctor, bi-directional MCP capabilities, and an integration with Dynatrace.

I was briefed by NetBrain about these announcements as part of NetBrain's sponsorship of the AutoCon 5 conference. Here's what I learned.

Doctor Doctor.

AI Path Doctor taps into the NetBrain digital twin to validate the path that a flow is taking. It checks ACLs, routing policies, next-hops, and other path information, and can highlight problems that affect performance to improve troubleshooting.

Context is king.

NetBrain is adding more network context to help make its agents more accurate and consistent in their diagnoses. With support for bi-directional MCP, NetBrain agents can get information from third-party sources that support MCP, such as ServiceNow. By gathering context from third-party sources, such as observability tools, your ITSM, and log repositories, the goal is to make the agents more accurate and consistent.

NetBrain isn't just consuming data; it can share its own network information with third-party agents via MCP. And as an MCP server, NetBrain can expose tools such as "find device" and "calcuate path" so that other workflows can call into NetBrain.

Application dependency for faster MTTI.

NetBrain now integrates with Dynatrace, an Application Performance Monitoring (APM) platform, to map dependencies between the network and critical applications. This dependency mapping can be very useful during troubleshooting or change management to see which applications rely on which network devices. This integration is meant to help reduce the finger-pointing that can occur between app and network teams when performance or connectivity problems arise.

Other new features include the Golden Assessment Library, or GAL. GAL is a repository of pre-built network automations built around industry-wide network knowledge gathered by NetBrain from its customer base.

Token budgets.

AI doesn't come free, and many organizations are running up against token budgets. I asked NetBrain about how it addresses token consumption. A NetBrain spokesperson provided the following information:

With each seat [license] we provide $120 tokens. Those tokens are used/available for all AI functions (Triggered or manual Deep Diagnosis, Runbook Companion, AI BOT, AI Help, etc.). After that it's passthrough billing. Example: Using the $120 AI usage credit, a customer could check the health of their entire network via AI about 245,000 times.

I appreciate NetBrain being clear about how it measures these costs.If you're attending AutoCon 5 in Munich, Germany, you can see NetBrain in action at their booth. And you can always find them online at netbrain.com.

About Drew Conry-Murray: Drew Conry-Murray has been writing about information technology for more than 15 years, with an emphasis on networking, security, and cloud. He's co-host of several podcasts on Packet Pushers including The Network Break, Packet Protector, and Heavy Networking. He's also a Tech Field Day delegate. He loves real tea and virtual donuts, and is delighted that his job lets him talk with so many smart, passionate people. He's also the author of the novels Wasteland Blues and The Haunting of Edward Drake.

Meet NetBrain: ALLIANCE Distribution signs distribution agreement with the leader in agentic netops.

ALLIANCE Distribution announces the signing of a distribution agreement with NetBrain, a leading vendor in AI-powered network operations automation that helps enterprises prevent outages and ensure the seamless operation of network infrastructure.

NetBrain solutions are now available through ALLIANCE Distribution for partners and clients in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan.

When network infrastructure becomes mission-critical, manual management is no longer enough.

Modern corporate networks span cloud environments, physical infrastructure, and software-defined networks simultaneously. Traditional approaches to network management - such as manual documentation, reactive troubleshooting, and siloed tools - cannot keep pace with the complexity and speed of change. Every hour of downtime costs organizations more and more.

NetBrain solves this problem with a unified, AI-powered network operations automation platform that enables organizations to:

* Gain full, real-time visibility into hybrid network infrastructure.
* Proactively identify risks and prevent outages before they occur.
* Automate diagnostics and accelerate troubleshooting by isolating issues without manual data collection.

About NetBrain.

NetBrain is a US-based network operations automation vendor trusted by major global enterprises, including US Bank, DXC Technology, BT, and New Balance. The company is recognized by Gartner analysts in the field of network operations and automation. The NetBrain platform combines artificial intelligence, no-code automation, and a live digital twin of the network into a single, production-ready solution.

Key capabilities of the NetBrain platform.

* Automated Network Discovery and Mapping: Automatically builds up-to-date maps of hybrid and cloud infrastructure, data paths, and documentation without manual effort.
* Network Digital Twin: A live virtual replica of the real network for analysis, testing, and diagnostics without risking the production environment.
* Automated Troubleshooting: AI detects the root cause of an outage at the moment the incident occurs, triggers diagnostic scenarios, and provides engineers with precise data for rapid remediation.
* Proactive Network Assessment: 24/7 monitoring of network compliance with specified criteria, detecting anomalies and risks before they cause an incident.
* Automated Change Verification: Analyzes the impact of planned changes on the network, verifying infrastructure status "before and after" to protect against unwanted deviations and prevent human error.
* No-Code Automation: A library of ready-to-use automation scripts that network engineers can adapt and run without programming skills.

Why this matters for central asia and the caucasus.

For organizations in the region, where network infrastructure forms the backbone of banks, telecom companies, government agencies, and industrial enterprises, network reliability and control are matters of operational continuity.

NetBrain enables network teams to shift from reactive incident response to proactive management: identifying problems before outages occur, reducing recovery time, and lowering the workload on engineers. According to the vendor, customers achieve up to a 90% reduction in recurring tickets and up to an 80% reduction in network troubleshooting time.

Get started with NetBrain today.

NetBrain solutions are now available to partners and clients through ALLIANCE Distribution.

Contact its team to:

* Get a demonstration and technical consultation.
* Evaluate how the solution fits your needs.
* Discuss partnership opportunities.

Business Wire

Published May 29, 2026

Article content

Newest expansion of the NetBrain platform delivers Agent Skills, AI Path Doctor, MCP Server, and expanded cross-domain integrations, extending the agentic capabilities already running in production at hundreds of enterprises.

Article content

BURLINGTON, Mass. - NetBrain Technologies, Inc. today announced major new platform features that advance Agentic NetOps from an emerging category to operational reality. NetBrain's clients are already deploying agents that are diagnosing and remediating issues across complex multi-vendor enterprise networks. These new features further extend the platform with new agent tooling, cross-domain context, and open interfaces for the broader agentic enterprise.

Article content

Article content

* A leading health insurer used NetBrain's Deep Diagnosis agent to diagnose and resolve a weeks old VPN connectivity issue in under five minutes.
* A large manufacturer resolved a critical device issue with a single prompt, isolating the root cause across the network path in under 20 minutes, saving hundreds of hours of engineer time, shrinking MTTR by more than 95%.
* A global telecommunications firm found NetBrain's context-grounded agents outperformed a stand-alone frontier LLM on a persistent firewall problem, delivering both the correct diagnosis and the specific commands to remediate.

Article content

"NetBrain is enabling our customers to achieve Agentic NetOps in production today," said Bernadette Nixon, CEO of NetBrain Technologies. "Our agents are not simply AI assistants, but act as operators that diagnose, decide, and act, governed by the verified network grounding our platform provides. We are delivering on both the innovative, purpose-built Agents and a platform to provide the trusted network context that allows our customers to pursue automation confidently."

Article content

Why Agentic NetOps, and why now

Article content

Networks are where most enterprises place blame first for issues, and where AI built on event correlation alone consistently fails. Agentic NetOps requires more than inference: it requires verified, current network state, intent validation, and path intelligence that no telemetry stream can produce. Gartner(R) predicts that, "By the end of 2027, 80% of network automation platform vendors will introduce agentic AI capabilities that enable probabilistic automation, up from less than 20% in early 2026."*

Article content

NetBrain's network context model spanning Device, Topology, Path, and Intent across 150+ hardware vendors is the proprietary foundation that makes autonomous network operations possible. Available June 1, these new features extend the NetBrain platform:

Article content

* AI Path Doctor: Validates network paths, flags inaccuracies, and generates runbooks to remediate. Reliable paths are the precondition for every diagnosis and automation the agents run.
* Agent Skills: Institutional knowledge and best practices captured as Agent Skills tailoring NetBrain Agents to each customer's environment - without writing code or retraining models.
* Cross-Domain Context: New integrations consume application and infrastructure context from ITSM, security, and APM platforms, including Dynatrace, into NetBrain's diagnosis workflow, resolving the "is it the network or the application" question and eliminating 40% or more of tickets.
* Golden Assessment Library 26.06: Pre-built, industry-validated network assessments released on a regular basis to help stay abreast of industry shifts. This release includes updated coverage for capacity management, Cisco ACI intent integration with Deep Diagnosis, and Troubleshooting Skills for Deep Diagnosis.
* LLM Flexibility and MCP Support: Native support for Claude, Gemini, GPT, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including self-hosted models. Through MCP, NetBrain's network intelligence is now available to the broader agentic enterprise, extending NetBrain's grounded truth to whatever AI platforms our customers operate alongside it.

Article content

Article content

"The agentic conversation has been dominated by model choice and agent design and on ticket and log analysis use cases. The key to unlock adoption is grounded network truth that informs diagnosis and a remediation plan - for a real fix to real customer problems," said Song Pang, CTO of NetBrain Technologies. "Agent Skills tailor our agents to each customer's environment. AI Path Doctor guarantees path accuracy. MCP ties in the rest of the AI ecosystem. Together, they enable immediate business value and close the loop from diagnosis to remediation, at machine speed, with human confidence."

Article content

"Agentic NetOps software goes beyond assistants and chatbots that retrieve and suggest but depend on humans to decide what actions to take. Agentic network operations software interprets goals, plans, reasons, acts, and verifies under guardrails."**

Article content

NetBrain's Deep Diagnosis and Runbook Companion agents, released earlier this year, are deployed at hundreds of enterprises automating fault isolation and guided remediation. Both are now significantly more capable through MCP and Agent Skills, and the expanded platform foundation accelerates NetBrain's delivery of additional agents on the roadmap.

Customers leverage NetBrain from planning to change to day-2 network operations, employing human-in-the-loop to human-on-the-loop to human-out-of-the-loop diagnosis, assessment, and change. Extending NetBrain with NetBox and Grafana: Turning Operational Truth into Shared Insight.

* Home
* Blog
* Turning Operational Truth Into Shared Insight

by Nigel Hickey Feb 24, 2026

Modern network environments don't live in a single system.

Network teams operate in real time. Hardware and facilities teams manage physical infrastructure. Platform and operations teams need dashboards they can trust without giving every user access to deep operational tools.

NetBrain sits at the center of this reality.

At NetBrain LIVE 2025, one of its engineers walked through a live demo showing how NetBrain integrates cleanly with NetBox and Grafana. Not to replace them, but to extend NetBrain's real-time operational truth into existing ecosystems, customers already rely on.

This post breaks down what was demonstrated, why it matters, and how the integration works in practice.

NetBrain as the operational source of truth.

NetBrain's role is clear:
it continuously collects live data from network devices, validates behavior, detects drift, and drives automation.

That real-time digital twin is what allows NetBrain to answer questions like:

* What is actually happening on the network right now?
* Is this device configured correctly?
* Why did this change break something?

Things like:

* Physical rack position
* Airflow direction
* PDU and power details
* Facility-level metadata

That information is typically owned by hardware or data center teams and often already maintained in tools like NetBox.

Rather than forcing customers to rebuild that data model inside NetBrain, the integration shown at NetBrain LIVE takes a more pragmatic approach.

Using NetBox for what it does best.

In the demo, NetBox was used as a reference system for physical and static infrastructure data.

Hardware teams populate NetBox the same way they always have:

* Devices are racked
* Metadata is entered
* Power, airflow, and location details are documented

A NetBrain Plugin for NetBox then pulls that information into NetBrain via the NetBox API, mapping it into NetBrain custom properties and attaching it to the corresponding devices inside NetBrain. This is a NetBrain-built plugin that utilizes the NetBox API to pull hardware installation metadata into NetBrain.

The key point from engineering:

NetBox remains the source of truth for hardware installation data. NetBrain becomes the source of truth for the network itself.

No workflows change for the hardware team. No duplicate data entry is required. NetBrain simply consumes and enriches that data with live network context.

How the integration works (engineer walkthrough).

The demo showed a simple but powerful flow:

* NetBox holds physical device data
Rack position, airflow, and other properties are entered by the hardware team.
* NetBrain utilizes the NetBox API to pull that data into NetBrain
The data is mapped into NetBrain custom properties and populated into an ADT (Automation Data Table).
* The ADT table updates on a schedule
This process is automated and human-less - no manual refresh required.
* Grafana consumes the data automatically
Using a lightweight trigger and API-based access, Grafana scrapes the updated table and refreshes dashboards in real time.

During the demo, a device initially showed no physical metadata.
Once the table was rebuilt, the data appeared instantly and the Grafana dashboard updated from red to green without a manual refresh.

That moment captured the value clearly:
NetBox data | NetBrain context | Grafana visibility.

Why Grafana matters in this architecture.

Grafana plays a critical but specific role.

Not every user needs or should have direct access to NetBrain or NetBox.

Grafana becomes the shared visualization layer, allowing:

* Read-only access for broader teams
* Secure exposure of validated data
* A single dashboard view that blends physical and network truth

Instead of giving hundreds of users accounts in operational tools, teams can expose NetBrain-validated data through Grafana, ensuring everyone sees the same trusted information.

As discussed in the session:

Grafana makes the data accessible to everyone without making everyone an operator.

Complementary by design, not redundant.

One theme came through clearly in the engineer discussion:
this is not a competitive story - it's an architectural one.

NetBox excels at static infrastructure modeling.
NetBrain excels at live network intelligence and automation.

NetBrain can model physical properties if needed but when customers already have that data in NetBox, it makes more sense to leverage it rather than rebuild it.

The result:

* No disruption to existing processes
* Faster time to value
* A unified source of truth powered by live network data

Or as one engineer summarized:

If you already have the data, bring it into NetBrain.
Now you have the complete picture.

The bigger outcome: one truth, many consumers.

This integration pattern solves a real operational challenge:

* Hardware teams keep using NetBox
* Network teams rely on NetBrain
* Operations and leadership consume insights through Grafana

All backed by NetBrain as the authoritative, real-time engine.

The value isn't just integration, it's confidence.
Confidence that dashboards reflect reality.
Confidence that static data is tied to live behavior.
Confidence that automation decisions are based on truth, not assumptions.

Final takeaway.

NetBrain doesn't ask customers to rip and replace.

Instead, it:

* Pulls in the data you already trust
* Enriches it with live network intelligence
* Exposes it cleanly to the tools your teams already use

That's what was demonstrated at NetBrain LIVE 2025 and that's what modern network operations require.
